rows: All three fixtures routed through prove_unsat_to_lean_module emit a module naming the constructed carrier and not the axiomatized one.

kind.text: Counts rather than greps: `grep -q` would pass on ONE surviving fixture if the other two regressed or were dropped, and the second test rules out a mixed result rather than inferring it from the first. The example decides the carrier by the module's carrier DECLARATION, because every `CReal.foo` name contains the substring `Real.foo` and a `contains("Real.lt")` test survives the flip unchanged -- one shipped test did exactly that and asserted nothing. The names in this paragraph are the OLD ones on purpose: ADR-0522 renamed the axiomatized package `Real` -> `AxReal` on 2026-08-19 precisely so that no such substring exists, and rewriting the sentence would erase the hazard it records. Two more sites were found that day by the rename alone, both green.

kind.text: The footprint SIZE is left free (2, 3, 5) because it is the query's own variables and hypotheses and legitimately differs per fixture; what is pinned is that none of it is carrier. Carrier is computed as the footprint minus the `axeyum.reconstruct.` namespace, which is where this route mints every axiom of its own, so the split cannot be gamed by renaming a carrier declaration.

summary.text: The self-contained Lean module the front door returns declares 3, 5 and 2 axioms -- the query's own variables and hypotheses -- against 15, 22 and 10 for the same refutations over the AxReal package.

caption.text: Evidence row the-emitted-module-declares-only-the-querys-own-axioms as recorded in the ledger

rows: The self-contained Lean module the front door returns declares 3, 5 and 2 axioms -- the query's own variables and hypotheses -- against 15, 22 and 10 for the same refutations over the AxReal package.

kind.text: The equality of the two counts is computed BY THE EXAMPLE, per fixture, over both carriers, and reported as its own verdict line -- a regex backreference was the first attempt and this host's `grep` does not support one, which would have made the row silently unrunnable. `grep -x` on the whole line including the trailing `true` because an unanchored match also accepts the `false` rendering. This row also refutes a claim recorded on 2026-08-18 in F:farkas-refutation-over-constructed-reals -- that a rendered module over CReal would emit the whole constructed development as axioms and defeat the claim. It does not: `write_lean_module_impl` emits every reachable inductive as a real Lean `inductive`, so the development contributes zero axiom lines and the module declares 3, 5 and 2 (the query's own) against 15, 22 and 10 over AxReal.

summary.text: The modules the flipped routes emit are accepted by the real Lean kernel, so the claim is not confined to this repository's own checker.

caption.text: Evidence row real-lean-accepts-the-module as recorded in the ledger

rows: The modules the flipped routes emit are accepted by the real Lean kernel, so the claim is not confined to this repository's own checker.

kind.text: awk rather than grep: `checked` MUST equal `modules` and `modules` must be nonzero, because the suite SKIPS itself when no `lean` binary is present and a row asserting only `failed=0` would pass on a host that checked nothing -- and this host's `grep` has no backreferences, so the equality cannot be written as a pattern. `END { exit ... }` with `NR > 0` also fails when the LEAN_CROSSCHECK line is absent entirely. Measured 2026-08-18 against lean 4.30.0: 77 of 77, 0 failed. This row is not decoration: the carrier flip initially FAILED it -- 5 of 77 modules rejected with `Unknown constant Int.natAbs`, because the renderer ordered an inductive by its own type while writing its constructors, which mention later definitions, inline. That defect is fixed in the same change and guarded by two kernel unit tests that need no `lean` binary.

summary.text: The example's four aggregate verdicts, and an exit status that depends on all four.

caption.text: Evidence row the-verdict-lines-and-the-exit-status as recorded in the ledger

rows: The example's four aggregate verdicts, and an exit status that depends on all four.

kind.text: Without `--require-axiom-free` the example exits 0 on a negative result, which is exactly the failure mode this ledger keeps finding; the flag is what makes the status depend on the finding. The four lines are counted, not grepped, so a dropped verdict is a failure rather than a quieter pass, and matched with `grep -x` including the trailing `true` so the `false` rendering of the same sentence cannot satisfy it.

kind.text: WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY, and the price. (1) The AxReal package is NOT retired: LraReconstructCtx::new still builds it, ProofFragment::IntFarkas still routes through it -- harmlessly, since that route abstracts the interface away and instantiates at the integer model -- and nat_axiom_inventory still reports `real: axiom=30`. This fact says the shipped LRA/SOS routes no longer use those axioms, not that nothing does. (2) The rendered Lean module declares only the query's own axioms (3, 5, 2) and real Lean accepts it, so `#print axioms` on the Lean side agrees with Kernel::axiom_footprint here. This CORRECTS a claim recorded the same day on F:farkas-refutation-over-constructed-reals, that a module over CReal would emit the whole development as axioms; the renderer emits reachable inductives as real `inductive` commands. Getting there required fixing a renderer ordering defect the constructed carrier exposed -- an inductive was ordered by its own type while its constructors, written inline, mention definitions emitted later -- which rejected 5 of 77 crosscheck modules. (3) The module grew from 2.4-41 kB to about 2.6 MB (66x-1069x), because it must now carry the whole N/Z/Q/setoid development. That is the measured cost of the axiom-free carrier and it has not been optimized -- render_lean_module_compact and render_lean_module_with_inductives are untried levers. (4) The default was shippable only because PreludeKey::CReal landed first: build_creal_prelude is 4.7 s per call in release and 0.067 s out of the template.
